sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Close Grip Bench Press is a compound pressing exercise that targets the triceps with significant secondary involvement of the chest and anterior shoulders.

Using a narrower-than-shoulder grip and tracking the elbows close to the ribs increases the demand on the triceps compared to a standard bench press.

It is a foundational accessory lift for building lockout strength on the bench press and developing upper-arm size.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Directly targets the triceps brachii
- Builds bench press lockout strength
- Engages the chest and anterior shoulders as supporting movers
- Allows heavier loading than most isolation triceps work
- Reinforces shoulder stability and scapular control
- Improves elbow extension power for pressing movements
- Excellent accessory lift for powerlifting and strength training

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Triceps Brachii

Secondary: Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoids, Forearms, Core

sections.heading: Set Up
sections.content:
1. Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and eyes under the bar.
2. Grip the barbell with hands about shoulder-width apart or slightly closer.
3. Engage the lats and brace the core.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Lift the bar from the rack with the help of a spotter if needed.
2. Hold the bar straight over your chest with the arms fully extended.
3. Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows and shoulders packed.

sections.heading: Lower
sections.content:
1. Lower the bar slowly toward your lower-mid chest.
2. Keep your elbows close to your body throughout the descent.
3. Allow the bar to lightly touch the chest in a controlled manner.

sections.heading: Press and Repeat
sections.content:
1. Press the bar back up by extending the elbows.
2. Drive through the palms and engage the triceps and chest.
3. Lock out the elbows at the top and repeat for the desired reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Flaring the elbows out wide
- Using a grip that is too narrow and stressing the wrists
- Bouncing the bar off the chest
- Lifting the hips off the bench
- Failing to lock out the elbows at the top
- Letting the shoulders shrug toward the ears
- Choosing a load too heavy to control

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Barbell with appropriate weight plates
- Bench press station with safety arms or rack
- Athletic shoes for foot traction
- Optional: Spotter for heavier sets
- Optional: Wrist wraps for joint support

sections.heading: Bar Adjustments
sections.content:
1. Set the rack height so the bar can be unracked with a slight bend in the elbows.
2. Position safety arms just below your chest height.
3. Grip the bar with hands about shoulder-width apart or slightly closer.
4. Keep the wrists straight and stacked over the elbows.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet flat on the floor, hip- to shoulder-width apart.
2. Torso: Lying flat with shoulder blades retracted and tucked.
3. Arms: Elbows tracking close to the ribs, not flared.
4. Shoulders: Packed and pressed into the bench.
5. Head: Resting on the bench, neutral neck.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Standard Bench Press: Wider grip with greater chest emphasis
- Close Grip Push Up: Bodyweight equivalent
- Tricep Skull Crusher: Lying triceps isolation
- Tricep Pushdown: Cable-based triceps isolation
- Floor Press: Limited-range pressing variation
- Dumbbell Close Grip Press: Neutral-grip variation

sections.heading: Close Grip Bench Press Variations
sections.content:
Barbell Close Grip Bench Press: Described here
Dumbbell Close Grip Press: Neutral-grip dumbbell variation
Incline Close Grip Bench Press: Bench inclined for shoulder emphasis
Decline Close Grip Bench Press: Bench declined for triceps emphasis
Smith Machine Close Grip Bench Press: Fixed-path variation
Tempo Close Grip Bench Press: Slow eccentric for hypertrophy

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Wrist Pain: Use wrist wraps or slightly widen the grip
Shoulder Issues: Keep the elbows tucked and shoulders packed
Elbow Pain: Reduce range of motion and lighten the load
Weight Too Heavy: Drop weight or use a spotter
Beginners: Start light to learn the elbow tracking pattern
Advanced: Add chains or bands for accommodating resistance
